saints.name: St. Catherine of Siena
saints.title: Virgin and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: A Dominican mystic of Siena whose letters and Dialogue moved popes, and who helped bring the papacy home from Avignon…
biography: Born at Siena on 25 March 1347, daughter of the dyer Giacomo di Benincasa, Catherine consecrated herself to God in childhood and at sixteen took the habit of the Dominican tertiaries, living three years in prayer in a little room of her father's house.

After her mystical espousals she left her cell to nurse the sick and serve the poor, and her counsel was soon sought by princes. At Pisa in 1375 she received the stigmata, invisible at her own prayer, and in 1376 she went to Avignon, where her pleading moved Gregory XI to return the papacy to Rome in January 1377.

Peacemaker in a divided Italy, she dictated at Siena her Dialogue of Divine Providence, and when the Great Schism opened in 1378 she gave herself wholly to Urban VI, who summoned her to Rome. There, spent by penance and by her labours for the Church's unity, she died on 29 April 1380, aged thirty-three.

Canonized by Pius II in 1461, she was named patroness of Italy in 1939, declared a Doctor of the Church in 1970, and made co-patroness of Europe in 1999; her nursing of the sick makes her a patron of nurses.
saints.knownFor: Recalling the popes to Rome and her mystical writings.

canonization.canonized: 1461 by Pope Pius II; Doctor of the Church (1970)
